column1: # M0 baseline: unported LuaJIT 2.1 (base 63c8f1a9) vs PUC-Lua 5.4.7, aarch64.
# Reasons are triaged by root cause and tagged with the phase that fixes them.

column3: P5: require/loadlib 5.4 protocol: NAME mismatch on arm64 (x64 passes); three-value loadlib when==absent
IMPL-DEFINED: long strings are interned in the fork, so gsub/concat %p identity differs (PUC does not intern long strings; needs lj_str.c)
IMPL-DEFINED: functional asserts pass; table.sort prints comparison counters/timings that differ from PUC
PERF: our side exceeds 60s (triage; raise timeout)
PERF: JIT-on side exceeds 60s while JIT-off finishes (mode A now passes; triage the slowdown)
P5: corpus lacks its built libs/*.so fixtures (PUC also stops there); progname/argv and traceback naming differ
P1: int64 numeric model + math library 5.4
P5: pattern semantics now match PUC except one %p identity assert (gsub returns interned strings; needs lj_str.c)
IMPL-DEFINED: dump/reload border bug FIXED and rawlen added; only the runtime-built sparse-table border differs (any border is legal per the 5.4 manual)
P1.8b: tail-call error names -- LuaJIT reuses the caller frame, so the loaded-module fallback reports 'string.rep' where 5.4 reports the short 'rep'. Non-tail and pcall paths match.
IMPL-DEFINED: runtime-built sparse tables may report any legal border (5.4 manual 3.4.7); LuaJIT's array-growth policy differs from PUC's alimit hint
FORK: private dump format (LuaJIT-5.4 fork); PUC 5.4.7 cannot round-trip it, mode R checks ours
